source_title: Heroes of Might and Magic III: The Restoration of Erathia
continuity: Heroes of Might and Magic III: The Restoration of Erathia original 1999 English PC release
description: The queen travelling to Erathia with an entourage. The manual identifies her as Nicolas Gryphonheart's grieving daughter and says she has not ruled out foul play in his death.

roles_and_vocations.note: Exact title used by the 1999 manual.

affiliations.note: The manual says the Commander travels among Catherine's entourage.

cosmologies_and_realms.note: The stated destination/land in the introduction.

canon_status: Named campaign-frame royal figure directly characterized in the original manual.

citations.locator: Player Manual printed pp. 4–5, Introduction: 'set sail with Queen Catherine' and 'grieving daughter'
supports: Catherine's name/title, travel to Erathia, entourage, Nicolas kinship context, and suspicion of foul play

comparison_cautions: The manual calls her Catherine/Queen Catherine but supplies no family surname; none is imported from a different title or edition.
Suspicion of foul play is Catherine's unresolved possibility, not a culprit or solved-mystery claim.

source_title: Heroes of Might and Magic III: The Restoration of Erathia
continuity: Heroes of Might and Magic III: The Restoration of Erathia original 1999 English PC release
description: The former king of Erathia, described by Wilbur as a great king and dedicated ally; the manual's opening frames his death as potentially involving foul play and identifies Catherine as his daughter.

roles_and_vocations.note: The manual calls him a great king.

affiliations.note: The manual names it as his realm of rule.

states_and_transformations.note: The manual directly calls his death; its cause is unresolved in this witness.

canon_status: Named deceased king directly characterized in the original manual's campaign frame.

citations.locator: Player Manual printed pp. 4–5, Introduction: 'Nicolas Gryphonheart's rule' and discussion of his death
supports: Nicolas Gryphonheart name, kingship of Erathia, allied characterization, death, and Catherine family context

comparison_cautions: The manual does not identify a murderer, cause of death, resurrection, appearance, or later plot outcome.
Only the 1999 Heroes III witness is used; names/claims from other Heroes or Might & Magic releases are not merged.
